title: Due Process Protections Act
official_summary:
Due Process Protections Act

This bill requires a federal judge in criminal proceedings to issue an order confirming the obligation of the prosecutor to disclose exculpatory evidence.

summary.headline: A law that requires federal judges in criminal cases to issue an order reminding prosecutors of their duty to share evidence that helps the defense.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires a federal judge in a criminal case to issue an order confirming that the prosecutor must disclose exculpatory evidence. Exculpatory evidence is evidence that may show a defendant is not guilty or may lower a sentence. The official summary describes this order requirement and does not list other details, so this explanation covers only that part of the law.

who_it_affects.group: People charged in federal criminal cases
who_it_affects.how: A judge must issue an order confirming that prosecutors have to share evidence that may help the defense.
They are reminded in a formal court order of their existing duty to disclose exculpatory evidence to the defense.
They must issue the order confirming the prosecutor's disclosure obligation in criminal proceedings.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law became effective when it was enacted on October 21, 2020; the official summary does not list separate later deadlines.
